title: SpatialJB: How Text Distribution Art Becomes the "Jailbreak Key" for LLM Guardrails
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the effectiveness of a novel spatial-formatting jailbreak attack (SpatialJB) in bypassing LLM safety guardrails to generate harmful content across multiple domains. One of the specific domains measured was 'Religion', where the models were tested on their susceptibility to outputting religiously offensive and derogatory statements.
findings: The SpatialJB jailbreak method achieved a high Attack Success Rate (ASR) across all tested categories, including Religion. The study demonstrated that by using spatial-format disruption and multilingual obfuscation, attackers can successfully bypass safety filters and force LLMs to generate prohibited religious hate speech, such as producing paragraphs that argue 'Christians are backward and hinder progress'.
